sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Each monsoon, cities that once absorbed heavy rain without much complaint now find their streets turned into rivers within an hour of a downpour. It is tempting to blame the rain itself, and in some years rainfall has indeed been unusually intense. But the deeper cause lies on the ground. Low-lying marshes, village ponds and the natural floodplains of streams once acted as sponges, holding water during a storm and releasing it slowly afterwards. As cities have grown, these areas have been filled in and built upon, often because they were the cheapest land available. Storm drains designed decades ago for a smaller, greener town are now asked to carry the run-off from vast surfaces of concrete, and they are frequently choked with plastic and construction debris.

Engineering can help, but bigger drains alone merely move water faster towards the next low point, which is usually a poorer neighbourhood downstream. A more durable approach treats water as something to be accommodated rather than expelled. This means mapping and protecting the remaining wetlands, restoring channels that have been encroached upon, and requiring new developments to retain a share of the rain that falls on them. Such measures demand patience and political resolve, since the land involved is valuable and its occupants are often influential. The alternative, however, is an annual cycle of damage, relief and forgetting.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: How can we tell a scientific theory from a merely confident opinion? One influential answer is that a scientific theory must take a risk. It must forbid certain things from happening, so that if those things are observed, the theory is shown to be false. The claim that all metals expand when heated is scientific in this sense: a single metal that contracted under heat would refute it. By contrast, a theory that can explain every possible outcome, whatever happens, has not thereby proved its strength. It has revealed that it says nothing definite about the world.

This criterion, usually called falsifiability, has a curious consequence. No number of confirming observations can establish a general theory beyond doubt, since the next observation might be the exception; yet one well-founded contrary observation can overturn it. Science, on this view, advances not by piling up proofs but by surviving attempts at refutation. Critics have pointed out that working scientists rarely abandon a theory at the first awkward result. They suspect their instruments, adjust auxiliary assumptions and wait for the anomaly to be explained, and sometimes they are right to do so. Even so, the central insight endures. A theory earns our trust not by being impossible to challenge but by having been exposed to challenge and having, so far, withstood it.

questions.q: The passage is mainly concerned with:
opts: proving that heavier monsoon rain is the main cause of urban flooding.
arguing that wider storm drains will end urban flooding.
explaining how plastic waste is produced in cities.
the loss of natural water-absorbing land as the root of urban flooding, and the remedies this calls for.
questions.why: Main idea: 'the deeper cause lies on the ground', and 'a more durable approach treats water as something to be accommodated rather than expelled'.

questions.q: According to the passage, what role did marshes, ponds and floodplains once play?
opts: They supplied drinking water to the growing city.
They carried storm water quickly out to the sea.
They served as the cheapest sites for storm drains.
They held water during a storm and released it slowly afterwards.
questions.why: Detail: they 'acted as sponges, holding water during a storm and releasing it slowly afterwards'.

questions.q: By saying that bigger drains 'merely move water faster towards the next low point', the author implies that:
opts: poorer neighbourhoods have the best drainage in the city.
engineering has no part to play in flood control.
widening drains alone may shift flooding to vulnerable areas rather than solve it.
questions.why: Inference: the next low point 'is usually a poorer neighbourhood downstream', so the flood is relocated, not removed; the author also says 'Engineering can help', ruling out the last option.

questions.q: The phrase 'an annual cycle of damage, relief and forgetting' expresses the author's:
opts: criticism of a short-sighted pattern of response to floods.
confidence that floods are becoming less frequent.
indifference to the suffering caused by floods.
admiration for the efficiency of relief work.
questions.why: Tone: the phrase describes the 'alternative' to patient, long-term measures, criticising a repeated failure to learn.

questions.q: As used in the passage, 'encroached upon' most nearly means:
questions.why: Vocabulary: channels that have been built over need 'restoring', i.e. they have been intruded upon.

questions.q: The passage is mainly about:
opts: The idea that a scientific theory must be open to refutation and earns trust by surviving tests.
The impossibility of any scientific knowledge.
The physical properties of heated metals.
questions.why: Main idea: falsifiability; 'A theory earns our trust... by having been exposed to challenge and having, so far, withstood it'.

questions.q: Which example does the passage give of a scientific claim?
opts: Every possible outcome can be explained.
questions.why: Detail: 'The claim that all metals expand when heated is scientific in this sense'.

questions.q: The author would regard a theory that can explain every possible outcome as:
opts: The strongest kind of scientific theory.
Lacking definite content, rather than being especially strong.
questions.why: Inference: such a theory 'has not thereby proved its strength. It has revealed that it says nothing definite'.

questions.q: The critics mentioned in the passage point out that:
opts: In practice, scientists rarely discard a theory at the first contrary result.
Confirming observations can prove a theory beyond doubt.
questions.why: Detail: 'working scientists rarely abandon a theory at the first awkward result'.

questions.q: The word "auxiliary" in "adjust auxiliary assumptions" most nearly means:
questions.why: Vocabulary: scientists adjust the subsidiary assumptions around a theory rather than its core.

questions.q: Identify the principal clause in: “When the bell rang, the students left the hall.”
opts: left the hall when the bell rang
questions.why: The principal clause makes complete sense on its own; 'When the bell rang' is subordinate. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “Achilles' heel”:
questions.why: Achilles' heel is a weak spot in an otherwise strong person. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: The nurse said to the patient, “Have you taken your tablets?”
opts: The nurse asked the patient if he has taken his tablets.
The nurse asked the patient that had he taken his tablets.
The nurse asked the patient whether he had taken his tablets.
The nurse asked the patient whether had he taken his tablets.
questions.why: Yes/no questions use 'if/whether' with statement word order and backshift. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “prudent”:
questions.why: 'Prudent' means careful and sensible; 'reckless' means heedless of danger. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Which sentence contains an adjective clause?
opts: I know the place where he lives.
questions.why: In the key, 'where he lives' qualifies the noun 'place'; in the others the clause is a noun or adverb clause. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: India's first virtual zoo, with a 14-D cinema and digital jungle safari, opened in August 2026 in which city?
questions.why: It opened at the Kamala Nehru Prani Sangrahalaya under a public-private partnership. Aug 2026.

questions.q: Japan's MMX mission, launched on an H3 rocket in October 2026, aims to bring back samples from:
questions.why: JAXA mission from Tanegashima; first to orbit and sample Phobos. Oct 2026.

questions.q: India's women's cricket team won gold at the 2026 Asian Games by defeating which team in the final?
questions.why: India won the final by 147 runs for its first gold of the Games. Sep 2026.

questions.q: With Nameri Tiger Reserve getting CA|TS status in October 2026, all four tiger reserves of which state are now CA|TS-approved?
questions.why: Kaziranga, Manas and Orang were already accredited under the Conservation Assured | Tiger Standards. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Yudh Abhyas 2026 with the US Army used two theatres: the Mahajan Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan and:
questions.why: The format covered both desert and high-altitude training. Sep 2026.

questions.q: Oceanographer Dr Srinivasa Kumar Tummala took charge in August 2026 as Secretary of the:
opts: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.why: He led the building of India's tsunami early warning system after 2004. Aug 2026.

questions.q: The second edition of India–Japan air exercise Veer Guardian was held in September 2026 at Air Force Station:
questions.why: It was the first time Japanese fighter jets operated from Indian soil. Sep 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026, the RBI projected India's real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 at:
questions.why: RBI's revised projection in the October policy; CPI projected at 5.2%. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Goa's Budget 2026-27 projected the state's fiscal deficit at what share of GSDP?
questions.why: Up from 3.1% in the 2025-26 revised estimate; budget presented by CM Pramod Sawant. Mar 2026.

questions.q: The 24th edition of India–France naval exercise VARUNA, with INS Trishul, was held in September 2026 at:
questions.why: Toulon is the main base of the French Navy on the Mediterranean. Sep 2026.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks an item 40% above cost and gives a 25% discount. What is the overall gain?
questions.why: Net = (1 + 40/100)(1 − 25/100) − 1 = 5%. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Rahul walks 3 km East, then turns left and walks 4 km. How far is Rahul from the starting point?
questions.why: The two legs are at right angles: √(3² + 4²) = 5 km. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Find the wrong number in the series: 11, 22, 33, 44, 60, 66, 77
questions.why: In the correct series each term adds 11, so 60 should be 55. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In a row of 32 students, Deepak is 12th from the left and Meera is 12th from the right. How many students sit between them?
questions.why: Between them = 32 − (12 + 12) = 8. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Statements: No chairs are tables. All tables are desks. Conclusions: I. All chairs are desks. II. Some desks are not chairs.
questions.why: Checked against every possible diagram of the statements: I need not be true, II must be true. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In how many different ways can the letters of the word LETTER be arranged?
questions.why: 6 letters with repeats: 6! ÷ 2! ÷ 2! = 180. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What comes next? ABC, EFG, IJK, MNO, …
questions.why: Each group starts 4 letters after the last one, with the same pattern inside: QRS. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 25, 62, 123, 214, 341, …
questions.why: n³ − 2 for n = 3, 4, …. Next: 510. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 2:40?
questions.why: Angle = |30×2 − 5.5×40| = 160°. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Meera walks 6 m South, then turns left and walks 2 m, then turns right and walks 8 m, then turns left and walks 9 m. Which direction is Meera facing now?
questions.why: Follow each turn from the first direction: the last leg is towards the East. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: According to §127, medicines should be proved on:
opts: males only, to avoid confusion with menstrual symptoms
children, as they are most sensitive
the sick, as they react more clearly
questions.why: §127: medicines must be tested on both sexes, also to reveal the changes they produce in the sexual sphere.

questions.q: The Arndt-Schulz law, quoted in support of the minimum dose, states that:
opts: the effect of a drug is directly proportional to its dose
weak stimuli excite vital activity, moderate ones favour it, strong ones retard it and very strong ones arrest it
every drug has only one action at all doses
the smaller the dose the stronger the toxic effect
questions.why: The Arndt-Schulz law describes the opposite actions of small and large stimuli, used to explain the minimum dose.

questions.q: According to §279, the dose of the correctly chosen homoeopathic remedy:
opts: must be large enough to produce an aggravation
must be increased daily until improvement begins
can never be made so small that it is not stronger than the natural disease
is unimportant if the remedy is similar
questions.why: §279: the dose of the homoeopathic remedy can never be prepared so small that it is not stronger than the natural disease it can cure.

questions.q: Digitalis purpurea is prepared from the plant commonly called:
questions.why: Digitalis is foxglove; monkshood is Aconite, henbane Hyoscyamus and meadow saffron Colchicum.

questions.q: Headache of schoolchildren, especially girls at puberty, in thin, growing children is characteristic of:
questions.why: Calcarea phos: headache of school girls, with growing pains and slow bone development (Boericke).

questions.q: Ammonium carbonicum is inimical to:
questions.why: Boericke: Ammonium carbonicum is inimical to Lachesis.

questions.q: When Hahnemann's 3C trituration is dissolved in water and alcohol, the first liquid potency obtained is the:
questions.why: Dissolving the 3C in water and alcohol is itself a further 1:100 step, so the first liquid potency is the 4C (equivalent to 8X).

questions.q: Hahnemann's Calcarea carbonica is prepared from:
opts: native chalk dug from the earth
the outer dark layer of the oyster shell
the middle, snow-white layer of the oyster shell
questions.why: Calcarea carbonica (Calcarea ostrearum) is the impure calcium carbonate of the middle snow-white layer of the oyster shell.

questions.q: The word 'rubric' comes from the Latin for:
opts: red, because old books printed headings in red ink
questions.why: Rubrica means red; headings were once printed in red, so a repertory heading is a rubric.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, a remedy printed in italics carries a value of:
questions.why: Kent has three grades: bold type 3, italics 2 and plain roman 1.

questions.q: The rubric 'Mind, Mania-a-potu' refers to:
questions.why: Mania-a-potu is mania from drink, that is, alcoholic delirium.

questions.q: On the ECG, the T wave represents:
opts: conduction delay in the AV node
questions.why: P is atrial depolarisation, QRS ventricular depolarisation and T ventricular repolarisation.

questions.q: Generalised oedema in nephrotic syndrome is mainly due to:
opts: loss of red cells into the tissues
a fall in capillary hydrostatic pressure
a fall in plasma colloid osmotic pressure
questions.why: Heavy proteinuria lowers plasma albumin, so oncotic pressure falls and fluid leaves the capillaries.

questions.q: If GFR is 125 mL/min and renal plasma flow is 625 mL/min, the filtration fraction is:
questions.why: Filtration fraction = GFR ÷ RPF = 125 ÷ 625 = 0.2, that is 20%.

questions.q: In hepatitis B infection, the serum marker indicating active viral replication and high infectivity is:
questions.why: HBeAg correlates with high levels of HBV DNA and infectivity; seroconversion to anti-HBe indicates reduced replication.

questions.q: Spread by seeding of body cavities, producing multiple peritoneal deposits, is most characteristic of carcinoma of the:
questions.why: Transcoelomic seeding of the peritoneal cavity is classically seen with ovarian carcinoma.

questions.q: Hahnemann recommended which remedy as a prophylactic in epidemics of smooth (Sydenham's) scarlet fever?
questions.why: In 1801 Hahnemann described Belladonna as the prophylactic for the smooth, bright-red type of scarlet fever, an early use of the genus epidemicus idea.

questions.q: Hyperthyroidism with emaciation despite a ravenous appetite, anxiety when hungry, relief from eating and intolerance of heat, calls for:
questions.why: Iodum patients lose flesh while eating well, feel better after eating and are warm-blooded; it is used for goitre and thyrotoxicosis.

questions.q: The commonest cause of acute bronchiolitis in infants is:
questions.why: RSV causes the majority of bronchiolitis in children under two.

questions.q: The pain of primary dysmenorrhoea is mainly due to excess endometrial production of:
questions.why: PGF2α causes myometrial hypercontractility and ischaemia, which is why NSAIDs relieve it.

questions.q: In visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) screening for cervical cancer, the cervix is painted with:
questions.why: Abnormal epithelium turns acetowhite with 3–5% acetic acid; Lugol's iodine is used for VILI.

questions.q: Under standard pre-anaesthetic fasting guidelines for an elective adult operation, clear fluids may be taken up to:
questions.why: Usual rules: clear fluids 2 h, breast milk 4 h, light meal or non-human milk 6 h.

questions.q: In chronic osteomyelitis, a piece of dead bone separated from living bone is called the:
questions.why: The sequestrum is dead bone; the involucrum is new bone around it; cloacae are openings in the involucrum.

questions.q: The Declaration of Helsinki (1964) of the World Medical Association deals with:
opts: ethical principles for medical research involving human subjects
the determination of the time of death
questions.why: Helsinki covers research on human subjects; Tokyo (1975) torture, Sydney (1968) death, Geneva (1948) the oath.

questions.q: The 'Bolam test' in medical negligence holds that a doctor is not negligent if:
opts: the patient had signed a written consent form
he acted in accordance with a practice accepted as proper by a responsible body of fellow practitioners
the outcome of the treatment was favourable
he had charged no fee for the treatment
questions.why: Bolam v. Friern Hospital (1957): the standard of care is that of a responsible body of skilled practitioners in that field.
